title: Cuphead: Pip and Dot: conflicting faces on one body

people.name: Tina Nawrocki
people.role: Animator and designer of this character, identified in her own production post

summary: Two faces share a rectangular body but carry different attitudes.

observations.text: In the idle drawing, the upper face bares clenched teeth while the lower face grins. Their sideways pupils establish attitude inside a stable rectangular silhouette.
The hat drawings contrast lowered lids with sharply angled brows and broader grins. The hat and bow distinguish the two faces.
The mouth-attack drawing separates the domino halves and exposes large teeth while the small faces remain legible.

mistIdeas: Our inference: try an asymmetric MIST listening pose with one lid lower and a restrained mouth.
Our inference: fix two or three identity anchors while the lids and mouth carry a reaction.

title: Cuphead: Hopus Pocus: mouth shapes that change the character

people.name: Tina Nawrocki
people.role: Animator of Hopus Pocus, identified in her own production post

summary: A small two-tooth smile and a predatory grin feel different while preserving the same rabbit.

observations.text: The first attack drawing has a small mouth and two front teeth beneath narrowed, offset eyelids. Other drawings expose a long serrated grin and larger eye openings.
The smear drawing stretches head and hands together. Nose, eye masses and grin remain grouped rather than moving as unrelated parts.
The death drawing stretches the neck and pulls the eyes into unequal vertical shapes; nose and ears still identify the rabbit.

mistIdeas: Our inference: draw different mouth silhouettes for interest, delight and alarm rather than scaling one oval.
Our inference: test one coordinated facial distortion followed by a return to the neutral layout; these stills do not establish its duration.

title: Cuphead: Baroness Von Bon Bon: theatrical facial extremes

people.name: Tina Nawrocki
people.role: Animator and designer of this character, identified in her own production post

summary: Closed eyes, an open jaw, a clenched grin and startled eyes demonstrate distinct emotional drawings.

observations.text: The compact pose combines closed eyelids with a tiny heart-like mouth. Another drawing expands the jaw and makes the two eyes unequal.
The detached-head drawing uses inward-angled lids and a broad toothy mouth. Spiral hair and the conical hat preserve identity.
The leaning drawing opens both eyes while keeping the mouth small. Face and extended arms jointly establish the reaction.

mistIdeas: Our inference: approve an expression sheet with distinct mouth and lid drawings before interpolating motion.
Our inference: support a readable facial reaction with a small head movement rather than animating every feature constantly.
